segments.source: Vancouver Swiss Water Decaf is Verve's named whole-bean blend, separate from its Vancouver craft-instant product. The current US page calls the beans medium roast, 6/10, and names Colombia and Uganda as origins. It does not disclose fixed farms, varieties, processing of each component or a permanent proportion, so those should not be inferred from the recurring blend name.
segments.context: Vancouver Swiss Water Decaf is Verve's named whole-bean blend, separate from its Vancouver craft-instant product. The current US page calls the beans medium roast, 6/10, and names Colombia and Uganda as origins. It does not disclose fixed farms, varieties, processing of each component or a permanent proportion, so those should not be inferred from the recurring blend name. [1]

segments.source: Swiss Water identifies its water-based green-coffee decaffeination process and says it removes 99.9% of caffeine. Verve's product prose uses a different 99.99%-caffeine-free phrase. Neither page is a lab result for the bag or drink you receive. Decaf is a lower-caffeine choice, not a guarantee of zero caffeine.

Neither page is a lab result for the bag or drink you receive. Decaf is a lower-caffeine choice, not a guarantee of zero caffeine. [1] [2]

segments.source: Almond, honey and cola appear on Verve's package art; the product copy frames the blend as candied almonds against chocolate. These are flavor descriptors, not added ingredients or sensory results Coffeedant measured. They make Vancouver a more dessert-leaning candidate than a bright fruit-first decaf, subject to what the actual bag and brewing method produce.

Neither specifies a controlled common roast date, recipe or comparison set. Treat them as examples of personal preference and extraction uncertainty rather than a vote count or current-lot score.

segments.source: Verve's current Dwell start is 20 g coffee to 300 g water in about 2:20; Chemex is 45 g to 675 g in about 5:45; French press is 35 g to 500 g in about 5:00. They are roaster suggestions for three different brewers, not Coffeedant results. Start with the one you own and record grind and water.

segments.source: The current product panel does not publish an espresso dose and beverage yield. Some owners have pulled Vancouver as espresso, but their baskets and machines vary. If espresso is the primary use, dial the delivered bag separately; do not use the 1:15 Dwell ratio in a portafilter. Intelligentsia Decaf Black Cat has an explicit roaster espresso start if that documentation matters more.

segments.source: The live selector offered 12 oz, 2.2 lb and 5 lb. A 12 oz whole-bean pack is a proportionate first trial for someone who drinks decaf only some evenings. A larger bag may suit a decaf-first household after it knows how quickly the beans are consumed. Check the selected grind option and actual roast date when the shipment arrives.

segments.source: Verve says its coffee is roasted to order and ships within two business days. That policy cannot establish the delivered date or condition. Store opened whole beans sealed, away from heat and moisture, and grind before brewing. General storage advice cannot guarantee one universal flavor peak for this blend.

segments.source: Verve's US page displayed $22 with 12 oz and one-time purchase selected on November 9. It did not establish tax, shipping or a later checkout total. This review therefore asks you to check the current whole-bean price, selected size and delivered cost rather than promising a discount.

segments.source: The strongest value case is a decaf you will actually finish using its published filter starts. A process name by itself cannot predict taste or show that a larger pack will save money if part becomes stale. If the first bag is for espresso, include time and coffee used to find a suitable grinder setting in that decision.

segments.source: Make Vancouver first in your usual Dwell, Chemex or French press routine using the corresponding Verve start. Note how many decaf cups you actually drink in a week before buying 2.2 or five pounds. If espresso is the main job, dial the delivered beans with a separately recorded dose and yield; the filter ratio is not a portafilter recipe. Compare Decaf Black Cat when a published espresso start would save more guesswork.

Counter Culture Slow Motion carries a different cocoa-and-molasses brief with its own current blend record. Neither is a sensory winner over Vancouver on Coffeedant data.
